title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-07-16
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1966 Fillmore show, highlighted by blazing Cream Puff War, In the Pines and Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller transfer delivers crystal‑clear soundboard fidelity that lets listeners hear every nuance of this early Dead performance. The set bursts with psychedelic intensity – standout moments include a scorching Cream Puff War, an inspired In the Pines, and a searing take on Viola Lee Blues – while only minor tape edits (opening/closing cuts and a mic drop on Cardboard Cowboy) keep the experience essentially flawless.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising both performance and audio quality; only a few note minor issues, resulting in a very high weighted rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mix is described as pristine, crisp and full; minor complaints include cut opening/closing tunes and a mic failure on Cardboard Cowboy, but overall the transfer is considered a masterpiece.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows naturally through early‑Dead staples, with rare rippers like Cream Puff War and Viola Lee Blues providing peaks; the few edited tracks do not disrupt the overall momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers praise Jerry’s tone, Gibson guitar work and his surprising lead vocal on Cream Puff War.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is called ‘great’ with a cranked‑Marshall‑ish tone; some note his solid bass underpinning the early jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ/harp receives enthusiastic shout‑outs – “shrill on dat hammond” and “surf rockin’ those keys”.
